input.quote: Section 7.1 No Resignation. The Servicer will not resign as Servicer under this Agreement unless it determines it is legally unable to perform its obligations under this Agreement.
input.rationale: The Vendor side of this rule is satisfied and then some: Section 7.1 bars Cellco from resigning as Servicer except where it is legally unable to perform, and Section 7.3 requires it to keep performing until a Successor Servicer accepts engagement — better than the preferred position (no Vendor convenience right during the term). The customer side fails, however. Our only exit from the servicing engagement is Section 7.2, which requires a Servicer Termination Event (payment failure, material breach uncured for 90 days, or Insolvency Event) and vests the removal right in the Indenture Trustee at the direction of the Controlling Class, not in the Issuer or the Depositor; Section 8.3 otherwise runs the Agreement until the last Receivable is paid in full, settled, sold or written off. There is no termination-for-convenience right for us anywhere in the document (a full-text search for "convenience" returns only the headings clause at Section 10.10), and the term plainly exceeds 12 months. Under the detection guidance that absence is a deviation (missing behaviour) rather than a missing clause, since a usable termination architecture (Articles VII and VIII) does exist. Redline proposed (ok:true): a new Section 7.1A giving the Issuer, at the Depositor's direction, a 30 days' notice convenience termination right with no fee or penalty and a refund of prepaid Servicing Fees, plugged into the existing Sections 7.3–7.5 transition machinery so noteholder continuity is preserved; the fallback of 60–90 days' notice is offered in the comment. Noted but not separately flagged: the Optional Acquisition (Section 8.1) and Optional Redemption (Section 8.2) exits sit with the Class A Certificateholder, defined at p0668 as "the Originators or their designee" (i.e., the counterparty side), and are exercisable on only ten (10) days' notice. That is not a Vendor walk-away from service in the playbook sense — it requires the pool price to be "as agreed upon by the Class A Certificateholder and the Issuer" and requires the Notes, accrued interest, Make-Whole Payments and all other Issuer obligations to be paid in full — so we have not double-flagged the notice period.

proposal.summary: Add an Issuer right to terminate the Servicer for convenience on 30 days' notice, without penalty and with refund of prepaid Servicing Fees.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Article VII lets us remove Cellco only on a Servicer Termination Event (and then only through the Indenture Trustee), so we have no ability to exit this multi-year servicing engagement without cause. We have added a 30 days' notice termination-for-convenience right in our favour, with no termination fee and a refund of Servicing Fees prepaid for the post-termination period, dovetailed into the existing Successor Servicer machinery in Sections 7.3 through 7.5. If 30 days is too tight operationally, we can live with 60-90 days' notice.

ops.text: Section 7.1A Termination for Convenience by the Issuer. In addition to any other right of removal or termination under this Agreement, the Issuer, at the direction of the Depositor, may terminate the rights and obligations of the Servicer under this Agreement for convenience, in whole or in part, at any time upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the Servicer, the Owner Trustee and the Indenture Trustee, without payment by the Issuer or the Depositor of any termination fee, penalty, make-whole or other compensation, and the Servicer will refund any Servicing Fee paid in respect of the period after the effective date of such termination. Sections 7.3, 7.4 and 7.5 will apply to a termination under this Section 7.1A as if the Servicer had been terminated under Section 7.2(c).
